case: Protocol IV, Convention on Certain Conventional Weapons
about: Ban on blinding laser weapons
outcome: In force 1998-07-30; 111 parties listed; US consented to be bound 2009-01-21

case: In re LTI Marksman 20-20 (laser speed detector)
court: New Jersey Superior Court, Law Division
about: Reliability of a police laser speed gun as evidence
outcome: Readings admissible without expert testimony under stated conditions (day or night, light or moderately heavy rain, up to 1,000 feet); heavy rain, falling snow or longer range need expert testimony

about: Audience eye injuries after a festival laser show
outcome: 12 laser retinopathy patients reported; no legal outcome found

about: Hand-held laser pointers above 1 mW
outcome: Prohibited imports from 2008-07-01; 2012 review found no significant drop in reported incidents

about: Eye injuries at a festival
outcome: Attributed to audience laser pointers, not the show

case: FDA proposed amendment to the laser performance standard (FDA-2011-N-0070)
about: IEC 60825-1 harmonization; Class 1 limit for toy lasers
outcome: Proposed rule

about: 175 injury cases from cutaneous laser procedures, 1999-2012
outcome: Study finding: 42.9% involved non-physician operators; laser hair removal the most common procedure

about: Laser pointer aimed at a Fresno police helicopter in 2012; the helicopter was investigating reported strikes on an emergency transport helicopter for Children's Hospital of Central California
outcome: Convicted by a federal jury, December 2013; sentenced to 14 years on 2014-03-10

about: Co-defendant in the Rodriguez case
outcome: Convicted by the same federal jury; sentenced in 2014 to 2 years in prison, later revoked and replaced with 5 years' probation, as Courthouse News reports

about: A 29-year-old patron lost sight in one eye after a laser aimed at a mirror ball reflected into the audience
outcome: €80,000 settlement reported (second-hand, ILDA citing El Periódico)

about: Appeal of the interference conviction under 18 U.S.C. 32(a)(5) and (a)(8) and the sentence
outcome: Conviction and sentence on the 18 U.S.C. 32 count vacated; 39A count remanded for resentencing

about: Appeal of the 60-month resentence under 18 U.S.C. 39A (guidelines range 21 to 27 months)
outcome: Affirmed 2016-10-25 (unpublished memorandum)

case: FDA Safety Communication on two show projector brands
about: Projectors FDA said were sold without an approved variance or might lack required features
outcome: Recommendation against use; no final resolution reported

about: 167 refractive surgery cases, 127 LASIK
outcome: Study finding: 35.3% unfavorable to the defendant; inflation-adjusted mean award $1,287,872
Study finding: 53% of 36 known outcomes for the plaintiff; mean indemnity payment $320,975

about: Conformance with IEC 60825-1 Ed. 3 and IEC 60601-2-22 Ed. 3.1
outcome: Guidance: FDA does not intend to enforce matching US requirements for comparable clauses

about: Laser strike on a San Antonio Police Department helicopter, 2023-11-03
outcome: Guilty plea; 37 months

about: Two counts of aiming a laser at aircraft: two small planes, 2022-11-20; one pilot's eyes damaged
outcome: Sentenced 2024-01-05 to 8 months plus 3 years supervised release with addiction and mental health treatment; plea not stated in the release

about: Laser at a helicopter over Yeovil (2022-08-03) and an Airbus A320 descending toward Bristol Airport (2022-08-14)
outcome: Admitted two counts; sentenced 2024-04-11 to 4 months' imprisonment

about: Laser product standard built on IEC 60825-1 Ed. 3.0
outcome: Regulation published 2024-10-09, in force one year after publication

about: Laser aimed at a plane flown by a flight instructor carrying a minor student, 2023-11-25
outcome: Guilty plea (October 2024); 2.5 years plus 3 years supervised release

about: Laser aimed at two US Air Force F-16s
outcome: Guilty plea 2025-02-26; 9 days in prison plus 3 years supervised release, 2025-06-25

about: Green laser pointer aimed at a Las Vegas Metropolitan Police Department helicopter, 2025-01-02
outcome: Guilty plea to one count; sentenced 2026-07-29 to 9 months plus 3 years supervised release (government sought 21 months)

about: Noncompliant laser pointers, show projectors, toys and similar foreign-made products
outcome: Detention without physical examination for listed firms

about: Laser shone toward a moving helicopter
outcome: Guilty plea to two counts, the second recklessly or negligently endangering an aircraft; 4 months' custody for the laser offense

case: FAA civil penalties for laser strikes
about: Lasers aimed at aircraft, under 14 CFR 91.11
outcome: Up to $11,000 per violation; up to $30,800 imposed for multiple incidents
